title: Read the Label, Solve the Snack

callouts.label: Serving Information
callouts.hint: Plate and portion icons sit in the top-left label band.
callouts.description: Serving information tells what amount the rest of a label describes.
callouts.tip: Always start here before comparing nutrient amounts.

callouts.label: Servings in the Container
callouts.hint: Two package icons appear in the top-right band.
callouts.description: A package can contain more than one serving.
callouts.tip: The entire package and one serving may not represent the same amount.

callouts.label: Food Energy
callouts.hint: A lightning-bolt icon anchors the second band.
callouts.description: Food energy supports movement, growth, thinking, and body work.
callouts.tip: Energy is not a moral score.

callouts.label: Fats
callouts.hint: Avocado and nut icons anchor the fats region.
callouts.description: The fats line reports the amount in one serving.
callouts.tip: Fats provide longer-lasting energy and help absorb vitamins.

callouts.label: Carbohydrates
callouts.hint: Grain and fruit icons anchor the carbohydrate region.
callouts.description: The carbohydrate line reports the amount in one serving.
callouts.tip: Carbohydrates are a main source of ready energy.

callouts.label: Added-Sugar Clue
callouts.hint: Sugar cubes create a distinctive comparison target.
callouts.description: Sugar information helps compare sweetened foods and drinks.
callouts.tip: One clue should be considered with serving information and the whole context.

callouts.label: Protein
callouts.hint: Bean and egg icons anchor the protein region.
callouts.description: The protein line reports the amount in one serving.

callouts.label: Caffeine Clue
callouts.hint: Moon and alert shapes mark a caffeine investigation area.
callouts.description: Caffeine may interfere with sleep, heart rate, and calm focus in children.
callouts.tip: Ask an adult to help check unfamiliar drinks and snacks.

callouts.label: School-Day Snack Context
callouts.hint: Fruit, crackers, and water sit beside school supplies.
callouts.description: A useful school snack fits the time available, storage conditions, and the student’s needs.
callouts.tip: Labels provide evidence; fresh foods may not carry a label.

callouts.label: Active Afternoon or Long Outing
callouts.hint: Water, sandwich, trail mix, and a packaged snack sit beside outdoor gear.
callouts.description: Longer activity or time away may change hydration, storage, and energy needs.
callouts.tip: Choose based on the situation rather than a universal “best” snack.
